sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: The topic for today's show is one of the most difficult we've ever handled.
sentences.zh: 今天节目的主题是我们处理过的最棘手的话题之一。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: It's boredom.
sentences.zh: 因为是无聊。

sentences.en: And it's really hard to make boredom interesting.
sentences.zh: 而且要让“无聊”变得有趣真的很难。

sentences.en: Social scientists have been studying boredom for many years,
sentences.zh: 社会科学家研究无聊已经很多年了，

sentences.en: why people get stuck in boring jobs.
sentences.zh: 研究人们为什么会困在无聊的工作中。

sentences.en: But now imagine standing there all day long.
sentences.zh: 但现在想象一下整天站在那里。

sentences.en: I cannot imagine a more boring job.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象还有比这更无聊的工作了。

sentences.en: How to combat boredom.
sentences.zh: 如何对抗无聊。

sentences.en: The reason for more hot sauce is that lack of sensory stimulation from your environment
sentences.zh: 之所以需要更多的辣酱，是因为环境缺乏感官刺激，

sentences.en: that you're compensating for it by putting hot sauce on.
sentences.zh: 你通过添加辣酱来弥补这种缺失。

sentences.en: And the pernicious effects that boredom has on our lives.
sentences.zh: 以及无聊对我们生活造成的有害影响。

sentences.en: Boredom, some scientists say, creates a feeling of meaninglessness.
sentences.zh: 一些科学家说，无聊会产生一种毫无意义的感觉。

sentences.en: So keep listening.
sentences.zh: 所以请继续收听。

sentences.en: I promise you won't be bored.
sentences.zh: 我保证你不会感到无聊。

sentences.en: Really.
sentences.zh: 真的。

sentences.en: In Greek mythology, King Sisyphus is accused by the gods of being vain, avaricious, and egotistical.
sentences.zh: 在希腊神话中，西西弗斯国王被众神指控虚荣、贪婪和自负。

sentences.en: Upon his death, he's condemned to roll a boulder up a hill, watch it roll down the other side,
sentences.zh: 死后，他被惩罚将一块巨石推上山顶，再看着它从另一边滚落，

sentences.en: and then repeat the process for all eternity.
sentences.zh: 然后周而复始，永无止境。

sentences.en: Now, we've all been there, stuck in repetitious boring jobs, doing boring chores, getting bored in class.
sentences.zh: 我们都有过这种经历，困在重复无聊的工作中，做着枯燥的家务，在课堂上感到无聊。

sentences.en: Some time ago, I spoke with Peter Ubel from Duke University.
sentences.zh: 不久前，我采访了杜克大学的彼得·乌贝尔。

sentences.en: Along with a colleague, David Comerford, Peter studied why people get stuck doing boring work.
sentences.zh: 彼得与同事大卫·科默福德一起研究了人们为什么会困在无聊的工作中。

sentences.en: He asked me to think about applying to be a security guard at a museum.
sentences.zh: 他让我考虑申请做一名博物馆保安。

sentences.en: At the time, it might sound like a wonderful job.
sentences.zh: 当时，这听起来可能是一份很棒的工作。

sentences.en: I'd just stand there and do nothing, and they'd pay me for it.
sentences.zh: 我只要站在那里什么都不做，他们还会付钱给我。

sentences.en: Wow, that sounds great.
sentences.zh: 哇，听起来真不错。

sentences.en: But now imagine standing there, all day long, while people are walking by the museum enjoying themselves.
sentences.zh: 但现在想象一下，整天站在那里，看着人们从博物馆经过，享受着他们的时光。

sentences.en: You're not even allowed to really talk to them much.
sentences.zh: 你甚至不能真正和他们多说话。

sentences.en: I cannot imagine a more boring job.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象还有比这更无聊的工作了。

sentences.en: Peter says that when you're anticipating the kind of work involved in a job,
sentences.zh: 彼得说，当你预想一份工作所涉及的内容时，

sentences.en: you may think about it differently than when you're actually doing the job.
sentences.zh: 你的想法可能与你实际做这份工作时不同。

sentences.en: One rule of thumb we follow in applying for jobs, we often pick work that doesn't involve a lot of effort.
sentences.zh: 我们在申请工作时遵循的一条经验法则是，我们通常会选择不需要付出太多努力的工作。

sentences.en: The researchers ran an experiment with business students and told the students they had a choice between two jobs.
sentences.zh: 研究人员对商学院学生进行了一项实验，告诉学生他们可以在两份工作之间做出选择。

sentences.en: The first job would be to sit in the back row and do nothing.
sentences.zh: 第一份工作是坐在后排什么都不做。

sentences.en: They couldn't look at laptops or cell phones.
sentences.zh: 他们不能看笔记本电脑或手机。

sentences.en: They had to just look straight ahead.
sentences.zh: 他们必须直视前方。

sentences.en: We'd pay them $2.50 for that five minutes.
sentences.zh: 那五分钟我们付给他们2.5美元。

sentences.en: So, money for doing nothing.
sentences.zh: 所以，什么都不做就能拿钱。

sentences.en: Or?
sentences.zh: 或者呢？

sentences.en: Or they might end up solving word puzzles for the last five minutes, where they'd sit in the front row,
sentences.zh: 或者他们最后五分钟可能会去解字谜，他们会坐在前排，

sentences.en: and we asked them, how much would we have to pay you where you'd choose the word puzzle over sitting and doing nothing?
sentences.zh: 我们问他们，我们要付给你多少钱，你才会选择解字谜而不是坐在那里什么都不做？

sentences.en: And we found that the large majority of the students said we'd have to pay them more than $2.50 to solve the word puzzles.
sentences.zh: 我们发现绝大多数学生说，我们必须付给他们超过2.5美元，他们才愿意去解字谜。

sentences.en: Now, at one level, this makes sense.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，这说得通。

sentences.en: If someone asks you to work harder, they should pay you more.
sentences.zh: 如果有人要求你更努力地工作，他们就应该付给你更多的钱。

sentences.en: And yet, when we asked them, independently, which do you think would be more fun?
sentences.zh: 然而，当我们单独问他们，你认为哪一个会更有趣时？

sentences.en: They said the word puzzles.
sentences.zh: 他们说是解字谜。

sentences.en: When we actually finished the five minutes and asked them how much they enjoyed those five minutes,
sentences.zh: 当我们真正结束了那五分钟，问他们有多享受这五分钟时，

sentences.en: the people solving the word puzzles enjoyed the five minutes significantly more.
sentences.zh: 那些解字谜的人明显更享受这五分钟。

sentences.en: And yet, very few of them said, yeah, pay me $2 and I'd be happy to do word puzzles because at least I'll be having fun.
sentences.zh: 然而，很少有人说，好吧，付我2美元，我很乐意去解字谜，因为至少我能从中获得乐趣。

sentences.en: Peter calls this tendency of the students to avoid hard work, effort aversion.
sentences.zh: 彼得将学生们这种逃避艰苦工作的倾向称为“努力厌恶”。

sentences.en: And he thinks that this is one reason many people get stuck in boring jobs.
sentences.zh: 他认为这就是许多人困在无聊工作中的原因之一。

sentences.en: A simple rule of thumb, the fancy term is heuristic, led them astray.
sentences.zh: 一条简单的经验法则——专业术语叫“启发式”——把他们引入了歧途。

sentences.en: More effort should mean more pay is not always true.
sentences.zh: 付出更多努力就应该得到更多报酬，这并不总是正确的。

sentences.en: It isn't just guards who tell people not to touch the paintings who get bored at work.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是那些告诉人们不要触摸画作的保安会在工作中感到无聊。

sentences.en: Even jobs that most people would consider to be wildly exciting can be boring much of the time.
sentences.zh: 即使是大多数人认为非常令人兴奋的工作，在很多时候也可能很无聊。

sentences.en: Think about firefighters or soldiers.
sentences.zh: 想想消防员或士兵。

sentences.en: Also, astronauts.
sentences.zh: 还有宇航员。

sentences.en: Max Nestrak from the Hidden Brain team has the story.
sentences.zh: 来自《隐藏的大脑》团队的马克斯·内斯特拉克带来了这个故事。

sentences.en: When NASA sends astronauts into outer space, something strange happens.
sentences.zh: 当美国国家航空航天局（NASA）将宇航员送入外太空时，发生了一件奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: They use more and more hot sauce.
sentences.zh: 他们使用的辣酱越来越多。

sentences.en: Scientists at NASA got curious about this.
sentences.zh: NASA的科学家对此感到好奇。

sentences.en: One explanation?
sentences.zh: 一种解释是？

sentences.en: The absence of gravity causes physical changes in the body and that weakens your sense of taste.
sentences.zh: 失重会导致身体发生生理变化，从而削弱你的味觉。

sentences.en: Another idea?
sentences.zh: 另一个想法？

sentences.en: Small enclosed places like spaceships are really stinky.
sentences.zh: 像宇宙飞船这样狭小的封闭空间真的很臭。

sentences.en: Tabasco hides the smell.
sentences.zh: 塔巴斯科辣酱可以掩盖这种气味。

sentences.en: Then there's boredom.
sentences.zh: 然后就是无聊。

sentences.en: Now, it may be hard to imagine astronauts getting bored.
sentences.zh: 现在，可能很难想象宇航员会感到无聊。

sentences.en: But think about spending weeks looking at the same loose-hanging wires,
sentences.zh: 但试想一下，几周的时间里，看着同样的松垂电线，

sentences.en: the same floating co-workers, the same blue planet through the same small window.
sentences.zh: 同样的漂浮同事，透过同样的小窗户看着同样的蓝色星球。

sentences.en: That's where the Tabasco sauce comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是塔巴斯科辣酱派上用场的地方。

sentences.en: So one hypothesis for the reason for more hot sauce is that that lack of sensory stimulation from your environment
sentences.zh: 所以，需要更多辣酱的一个假设是，环境缺乏感官刺激，

sentences.en: that you're compensating for it by putting hot sauce on.
sentences.zh: 你通过添加辣酱来弥补这种缺失。

sentences.en: So yes, there's not a lot of colors in your environment,
sentences.zh: 所以没错，你的环境中没有太多色彩，

sentences.en: but you can have colors in your mouth.
sentences.zh: 但你的嘴里可以有色彩。

sentences.en: This is Kim Binstead.
sentences.zh: 这位是金·宾斯特德。

sentences.en: She's a professor at the University of Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 她是夏威夷大学的教授。

sentences.en: And she studies the psychological effects of long-term spaceflight.
sentences.zh: 她研究长期太空飞行的心理影响。

sentences.en: And this is a subject that's really important to NASA
sentences.zh: 这是一个对NASA非常重要的课题，

sentences.en: because they want to send astronauts to Mars in the next 20 years.
sentences.zh: 因为他们想在未来20年内将宇航员送往火星。

sentences.en: Binstead's job is to figure out how to keep the astronauts healthy.
sentences.zh: 宾斯特德的工作是找出如何保持宇航员健康的方法。

sentences.en: And she's found that boredom isn't just a psychological problem.
sentences.zh: 她发现无聊不仅仅是一个心理问题。

sentences.en: They don't eat enough.
sentences.zh: 他们吃得不够。

sentences.en: And they don't eat enough for a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 他们吃得不够有几个原因。

sentences.en: And boredom is one of them.
sentences.zh: 而无聊就是其中之一。

sentences.en: The food isn't appealing.
sentences.zh: 食物没有吸引力。

sentences.en: And that's okay for a short stay on the ISS.
sentences.zh: 在国际空间站短暂停留还可以。

sentences.en: But it's really not okay for the two and a half years or so of a Mars mission.
sentences.zh: 但对于大约两年半的火星任务来说，这真的不行。

sentences.en: That malnutrition could seriously affect astronaut performance.
sentences.zh: 这种营养不良可能会严重影响宇航员的表现。

sentences.en: So a few years ago, NASA launched a new project.
sentences.zh: 所以几年前，NASA启动了一个新项目。

sentences.en: Scientists built this 1,200-square-foot geodesic dome.
sentences.zh: 科学家们建造了这个1200平方英尺的测地圆顶。

sentences.en: It looks like a bubble on the side of a volcano in Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像夏威夷火山边上的一个气泡。

sentences.en: The idea is to simulate a Martian environment.
sentences.zh: 其目的是模拟火星环境。

sentences.en: NASA started sending groups of six volunteers to stay inside the dome for months at a time.
sentences.zh: NASA开始派遣六名志愿者组成的团队，在圆顶内一次居住数月。

sentences.en: Here, water is limited.
sentences.zh: 在这里，水是有限的。

sentences.en: When the volunteers want to see a website,
sentences.zh: 当志愿者想浏览网页时，

sentences.en: they have to submit a request to retrieve the page.
sentences.zh: 他们必须提交请求来获取页面。

sentences.en: And when they want to go outside, they have to put on a spacesuit.
sentences.zh: 当他们想去外面时，必须穿上宇航服。

sentences.en: What we looked at out the window was red rock.
sentences.zh: 我们从窗外看到的是红色的岩石。

sentences.en: It was Mars.
sentences.zh: 那是火星。

sentences.en: It looked like Mars.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像火星。

sentences.en: It felt like Mars.
sentences.zh: 感觉像火星。

sentences.en: It sounded like Mars.
sentences.zh: 听起来也像火星。

sentences.en: We explored lava tubes, which are caves created by lava,
sentences.zh: 我们探索了熔岩管，也就是由熔岩形成的洞穴，

sentences.en: which are also on Mars.
sentences.zh: 火星上也有这种洞穴。

sentences.en: And it was a Martian-like environment.
sentences.zh: 那是一个类似火星的环境。

sentences.en: Kate Green is a science journalist
sentences.zh: 凯特·格林是一位科学记者，

sentences.en: who spent four months living in this tiny dome with five others.
sentences.zh: 她和另外五个人在这个小圆顶里生活了四个月。

sentences.en: She wrote about her experience in Eon magazine.
sentences.zh: 她在《永旺》杂志上写下了自己的经历。

sentences.en: She says that before she went in,
sentences.zh: 她说，在进去之前，

sentences.en: she considered herself a person who never got bored.
sentences.zh: 她认为自己是一个从不感到无聊的人。

sentences.en: I go into this mission, and I'm pretty sure that I'm not going to be bored.
sentences.zh: 我参加这次任务时，非常确定自己不会感到无聊。

sentences.en: Well, things wear on you over the course of four months.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在四个月的时间里，事情会让你感到疲惫。

sentences.en: And by things, I mean a static environment.
sentences.zh: 我说的“事情”是指静态的环境。

sentences.en: We were talking to the same five people every single day.
sentences.zh: 我们每天都在和同样的五个人说话。

sentences.en: Our home was a white dome with puffy walls that didn't really change day to day.
sentences.zh: 我们的家是一个白色的圆顶，墙壁鼓鼓的，每天看起来都没什么变化。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题就在这里。

sentences.en: Astronauts don't like to admit they get bored.
sentences.zh: 宇航员不喜欢承认他们感到无聊。

sentences.en: There's a stigma to it because the government is spending literally millions of dollars
sentences.zh: 这有一种耻辱感，因为政府确实花费了数百万美元

sentences.en: to send you into outer space.
sentences.zh: 把你送入外太空。

sentences.en: Even Kim Binstead, the researcher, was reluctant to call it boredom.
sentences.zh: 即使是研究人员金·宾斯特德也不愿称之为无聊。

sentences.en: She says it's a mental lethargy from lack of stimulation,
sentences.zh: 她说这是一种因缺乏刺激而产生的精神萎靡，

sentences.en: which is, like, boredom.
sentences.zh: 这就像是无聊。

sentences.en: In addition to all the other scientific research NASA is doing,
sentences.zh: 除了NASA正在进行的所有其他科学研究外，

sentences.en: scientists like Binstead have been studying ways to combat boredom.
sentences.zh: 像宾斯特德这样的科学家一直在研究对抗无聊的方法。

sentences.en: You can't give astronauts hobbies,
sentences.zh: 你不能给宇航员提供爱好，

sentences.en: but you can build variety into their existing routines.
sentences.zh: 但你可以把多样性融入他们现有的日常生活中。

sentences.en: One possibility is cooking.
sentences.zh: 一种可能性是烹饪。

sentences.en: Right now, astronauts eat all pre-prepared meals.
sentences.zh: 目前，宇航员吃的都是预制餐。

sentences.en: Dehydrated vegetable protein, tortillas, peanut butter, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 脱水植物蛋白、玉米饼、花生酱之类的东西。

sentences.en: Now, if you're an astronaut and NASA gives you a frozen lasagna for your mission to Mars...
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你是一名宇航员，NASA给你一份冷冻千层面作为火星任务的食物……

sentences.en: It's a lasagna now.
sentences.zh: 它现在是千层面。

sentences.en: It's always going to be a lasagna.
sentences.zh: 它永远都会是千层面。

sentences.en: Two and a half years from now, it's still a lasagna.
sentences.zh: 两年半后，它依然是千层面。

sentences.en: But if I give you pasta and tomato paste powder
sentences.zh: 但如果我给你意大利面和番茄膏粉，

sentences.en: and some herbs and seasonings and some cheese
sentences.zh: 还有一些香草、调味料和一些奶酪，

sentences.en: and maybe some freeze-dried meat,
sentences.zh: 可能还有一些冻干肉，

sentences.en: you can combine those in a bunch of different ways
sentences.zh: 你可以用很多不同的方式组合它们，

sentences.en: to produce maybe even hundreds of different meals.
sentences.zh: 甚至可以做出数百种不同的餐点。

sentences.en: So that variety means that you get some sensory stimulation
sentences.zh: 所以这种多样性意味着你可以从食物的多样性中获得一些感官刺激。

sentences.en: from that variety in your food.
sentences.zh: 还有创造性的一面，

sentences.en: There's also the creative side,
sentences.zh: 找出组合这些食材的最佳方式，让它们变得美味。

sentences.en: figuring out what best way to combine those ingredients to make them tasty.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，宇航员在前往火星的途中是不会做饭的。

sentences.en: To be clear, astronauts are not going to be cooking on their way to Mars.
sentences.zh: 你不会在宇宙飞船里做饭。

sentences.en: You are not going to be cooking in a spaceship.
sentences.zh: 让我直接把这个选项排除掉。

sentences.en: Let me just take that right off the table.
sentences.zh: 我们所说的烹饪是在行星表面进行的。

sentences.en: The cooking that we're talking about would be on the planetary surface.
sentences.zh: 所以火星的重力比地球小，但它确实有重力。

sentences.en: So Mars has less gravity than Earth, but it does have gravity.
sentences.zh: 所以火星的重力比地球小，但它确实有重力。

sentences.en: So that is, you can keep the ingredients in the bowl.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你可以把食材留在碗里。

sentences.en: Whereas on the space station, your ingredients are going to float all over the place
sentences.zh: 而在空间站上，你的食材会到处漂浮，

sentences.en: and it's just not really possible to cook on the ISS.
sentences.zh: 在国际空间站上做饭根本就不现实。

sentences.en: NASA isn't going to get rid of pre-prepared food altogether.
sentences.zh: NASA 不会完全放弃预制食品。

sentences.en: Inside the bubble in Hawaii, Kate Green and the other Pseudo-Martians
sentences.zh: 在夏威夷的模拟舱内，凯特·格林和其他“伪火星人”

sentences.en: had both pre-prepared food and raw ingredients.
sentences.zh: 既有预制食品，也有原始食材。

sentences.en: On their cooking days, they got pretty creative.
sentences.zh: 在他们轮到做饭的日子里，他们变得非常有创意。

sentences.en: They actually had a contest where people outside the bubble could recommend recipes.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至举办了一场比赛，让舱外的人推荐食谱。

sentences.en: They made a kind of sushi using Spam,
sentences.zh: 他们用午餐肉做了一种寿司，

sentences.en: patties out of flour and canned salmon,
sentences.zh: 用面粉和罐装三文鱼做成了肉饼，

sentences.en: and a crater crunch bar with quinoa flakes and macadamia nuts.
sentences.zh: 还用藜麦片和夏威夷果做成了“陨石脆脆棒”。

sentences.en: And cooking didn't just increase the variety of their diets.
sentences.zh: 而且烹饪不仅增加了他们饮食的多样性。

sentences.en: So many interesting things happen when you're preparing a meal,
sentences.zh: 当你准备一顿饭时，会发生许多有趣的事情，

sentences.en: especially with other people.
sentences.zh: 尤其是和其他人一起的时候。

sentences.en: Cooking is truly a social experience.
sentences.zh: 烹饪确实是一种社交体验。

sentences.en: I remember I had a number of great cooking experiences
sentences.zh: 我记得我确实和全体船员有过几次很棒的烹饪经历，

sentences.en: with everyone on the crew, actually.
sentences.zh: 真的。

sentences.en: Everyone had such different styles,
sentences.zh: 每个人的风格都大不相同，

sentences.en: and so it was a time when even if I wasn't working with people in a scientific way
sentences.zh: 所以即使我没有在科学层面与大家共事，

sentences.en: or with any of our projects,
sentences.zh: 或者没有参与任何项目，

sentences.en: I worked with everyone in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 我也会在厨房里和大家一起工作。

sentences.en: And that was, you really got to know a person's personality and attitude,
sentences.zh: 那真的能让你深入了解一个人的个性和态度，

sentences.en: and I really enjoyed that part of it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很享受那一部分。

sentences.en: Now there are other benefits to sending astronauts to Mars with ingredients
sentences.zh: 现在，让宇航员带着食材去火星，

sentences.en: rather than pre-prepared meals.
sentences.zh: 而不是带预制餐，还有其他好处。

sentences.en: Cooking with ingredients can be healthier.
sentences.zh: 用食材烹饪可以更健康。

sentences.en: It weighs less to send the food this way,
sentences.zh: 以这种方式运送食物重量更轻，

sentences.en: but there are costs.
sentences.zh: 但也有代价。

sentences.en: More equipment, more energy, and more astronaut time.
sentences.zh: 需要更多的设备、更多的能源，以及宇航员更多的时间。

sentences.en: There are more important things to do on Mars than make a homemade lasagna.
sentences.zh: 在火星上，有比做家常千层面更重要的事情要做。

sentences.en: But Binstead is finding the psychological benefits are worth the trade-off.
sentences.zh: 但宾斯特德发现，心理上的益处足以抵消这些代价。

sentences.en: If you look at the same things every day,
sentences.zh: 如果你每天都看着同样的东西，

sentences.en: if you eat the same things every day,
sentences.zh: 如果你每天都吃同样的东西，

sentences.en: it can produce some negative psychological effects.
sentences.zh: 这可能会产生一些负面的心理影响。

sentences.en: The creativity of making food
sentences.zh: 制作食物的创造力，

sentences.en: and the way you can use the same set of ingredients
sentences.zh: 以及你可以利用同一套食材，

sentences.en: in different ways to produce different meals,
sentences.zh: 以不同的方式做出不同的饭菜，

sentences.en: that those things were very psychologically important to the crew.
sentences.zh: 这些对船员来说在心理上非常重要。

sentences.en: NASA is running its fourth and final pseudo-Mars mission in Hawaii now.
sentences.zh: NASA 目前正在夏威夷进行第四次也是最后一次模拟火星任务。

sentences.en: Volunteers will be there an entire year.
sentences.zh: 志愿者们将在那里待上一整年。

sentences.en: That's Max Nestrak.
sentences.zh: 那是马克斯·内斯特拉克。

sentences.en: You can learn more about the pseudo-Mars missions
sentences.zh: 你可以访问 highseas.org，

sentences.en: by going to highseas.org.
sentences.zh: 了解更多关于模拟火星任务的信息。

sentences.en: That's H-I-S-E-A-S dot org.
sentences.zh: 网址是 H-I-S-E-A-S 点 org。

sentences.en: Coming up, Daniel Pink is here to play Stopwatch Science with me.
sentences.zh: 接下来，丹尼尔·平克将和我一起进行“秒表科学”环节。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about the pernicious effects of boredom in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论无聊对我们生活产生的有害影响。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Back now for another round of Stopwatch Science,
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到“秒表科学”环节，

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm joined as always by Daniel Pink.
sentences.zh: 和我在一起的依然是丹尼尔·平克。

sentences.en: He's been variously called the love guru and the divorce doctor.
sentences.zh: 他曾被戏称为“爱情大师”和“离婚博士”。

sentences.en: But on this show,
sentences.zh: 但在本节目中，

sentences.en: his primary title is Senior Stopwatch Science Correspondent.
sentences.zh: 他的主要头衔是“秒表科学高级通讯员”。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dan.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，丹。

sentences.en: Thank you, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: On Stopwatch Science,
sentences.zh: 在“秒表科学”中，

sentences.en: Dan and I give one another 60 seconds
sentences.zh: 丹和我给对方 60 秒的时间，

sentences.en: to summarize interesting social science research.
sentences.zh: 来总结有趣的社会科学研究。

sentences.en: As we approach the 60-second mark,
sentences.zh: 当我们接近 60 秒大关时，

sentences.en: our producers will bring up the music to drown us out
sentences.zh: 我们的制片人会放出音乐来淹没我们的声音，

sentences.en: just like they do at the Oscars.
sentences.zh: 就像他们在奥斯卡颁奖典礼上做的那样。

sentences.en: And they have itchy fingers,
sentences.zh: 他们可是迫不及待了，

sentences.en: so they are dying to do this.
sentences.zh: 所以他们非常想这么做。

sentences.en: Our topic today is boredom.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的主题是无聊。

sentences.en: Now, I often feel like my life is one long struggle to avoid being bored.
sentences.zh: 我经常觉得我的生活就是一场避免无聊的漫长斗争。

sentences.en: I hate being bored.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌无聊。

sentences.en: Are you the same, Dan?
sentences.zh: 你也是吗，丹？

sentences.en: Only when I'm with you, strangely.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，只有和你在一起的时候才会。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我不明白为什么。

sentences.en: Is that because you're talking to me or because you're listening to yourself?
sentences.zh: 是因为你在和我说话，还是因为你在听你自己说话？

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So today we're going to talk about the effects of boredom
sentences.zh: 所以今天我们要讨论无聊的影响，

sentences.en: and the lengths we're willing to go to avoid being bored.
sentences.zh: 以及我们为了避免无聊愿意付出多大的努力。

sentences.en: Dan, if you're ready,
sentences.zh: 丹，如果你准备好了，

sentences.en: your first 60 seconds starts now.
sentences.zh: 你的第一个 60 秒现在开始。

sentences.en: Okay, this research, published in Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin,
sentences.zh: 好的，这项发表在《人格与社会心理学公报》上的研究，

sentences.en: takes us to Ireland,
sentences.zh: 把我们带到了爱尔兰，

sentences.en: where a bitter history has left some Irish with a negative view of the English.
sentences.zh: 那里痛苦的历史让一些爱尔兰人对英国人持有负面看法。

sentences.en: Researchers gathered Irish university students and cafe-goers
sentences.zh: 研究人员召集了爱尔兰大学生和咖啡馆常客，

sentences.en: and divided them into two groups.
sentences.zh: 并将他们分成两组。

sentences.en: One group they bored the heck out of
sentences.zh: 他们让其中一组人感到极其无聊，

sentences.en: by making them count tiny boxes on computer screens
sentences.zh: 让他们长时间地数电脑屏幕上的小方块，

sentences.en: or draw lines on paper for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 或者在纸上画线。

sentences.en: The other group did the same tasks, but only briefly.
sentences.zh: 另一组人做了同样的任务，但时间很短。

sentences.en: Then they had participants play judge.
sentences.zh: 然后让他们扮演法官。

sentences.en: Researchers presented a hypothetical case about an Englishman beating up an Irishman
sentences.zh: 研究人员提出了一个假设案例，关于一个英国人殴打了一个爱尔兰人，

sentences.en: and asked participants what prison sentence they'd impose.
sentences.zh: 并询问参与者他们会判处多长的刑期。

sentences.en: Those who were deeply bored imposed far longer sentences than those who weren't bored.
sentences.zh: 那些感到非常无聊的人判处的刑期远比不无聊的人要长。

sentences.en: Then researchers reversed the scenario.
sentences.zh: 然后研究人员反转了场景。

sentences.en: An Irishman beats up an Englishman.
sentences.zh: 一个爱尔兰人殴打了一个英国人。

sentences.en: This time, the bored people gave their fellow Irishmen a shorter sentence
sentences.zh: 这一次，无聊的人给他们的爱尔兰同胞判处的刑期，

sentences.en: than people who weren't bored.
sentences.zh: 比不无聊的人要短。

sentences.en: Boredom, some scientists say, creates a feeling of meaninglessness.
sentences.zh: 一些科学家说，无聊会产生一种毫无意义的感觉。

sentences.en: When we feel things are meaningless, we seek meaning,
sentences.zh: 当我们感到事情毫无意义时，我们就会寻求意义，

sentences.en: and one way we do that is by aligning more closely with our own tribe
sentences.zh: 而我们这样做的一种方式，就是更紧密地与我们自己的群体靠拢，

sentences.en: and discriminating against those we perceive as outsiders.
sentences.zh: 并歧视那些我们视为局外人的人。

sentences.en: So that's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: What you're saying is that the more bored the Irish volunteers got,
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，爱尔兰志愿者越无聊，

sentences.en: the more willing they were to give English defendants a longer sentence
sentences.zh: 他们就越愿意给英国被告判处更长的刑期，

sentences.en: and Irish defendants a shorter sentence.
sentences.zh: 而给爱尔兰被告判处更短的刑期。

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And the people who weren't bored, though,
sentences.zh: 但是那些不无聊的人，

sentences.en: they gave the English and the Irish similar sentences.
sentences.zh: 他们给英国人和爱尔兰人判处的刑期差不多。

sentences.en: But there's something about being bored that makes us feel a lack of meaning.
sentences.zh: 但无聊确实会让我们感到缺乏意义。

sentences.en: And one way, unfortunately, the human beings seek meaning
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，人类寻求意义的一种方式，

sentences.en: is by affiliating with the in-group and discriminating against an out-group.
sentences.zh: 就是通过加入内群体并歧视外群体。

sentences.en: So do you think this has applications in the criminal justice system?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为这在刑事司法系统中有什么应用吗？

sentences.en: Perhaps.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that if you've ever been on a jury,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为如果你曾经担任过陪审员，

sentences.en: jury service is often quite boring.
sentences.zh: 陪审员的工作通常是非常无聊的。

sentences.en: And what this paper made me wonder is,
sentences.zh: 而这篇论文让我想到的是，

sentences.en: is being so bored serving on a jury introducing bias,
sentences.zh: 在担任陪审员时感到如此无聊，是否引入了偏见，

sentences.en: even more bias, into the criminal justice system?
sentences.zh: 甚至更多的偏见，进入了刑事司法系统？

sentences.en: But interesting question.
sentences.zh: 真是个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Let's go to you, Shankar, for our next one.
sentences.zh: 让我们转向你，尚卡尔，进行下一个环节。

sentences.en: Your 60 seconds starts right now.
sentences.zh: 你的 60 秒现在开始。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think that last study, Dan, was by Wynan Van Tilburg.
sentences.zh: 丹，我想上一项研究是温南·范·蒂尔堡做的。

sentences.en: Van Tilburg seems to be very interested in boring stuff
sentences.zh: 范·蒂尔堡似乎对无聊的事情非常感兴趣，

sentences.en: because I came by another study he did about boredom in 2013.
sentences.zh: 因为我偶然发现了他在 2013 年做的另一项关于无聊的研究。

sentences.en: Along with Eric Igu, Van Tilburg asked people to copy boring passages from Wikipedia
sentences.zh: 范·蒂尔堡和埃里克·伊古一起，让人们抄写维基百科上关于如何混合水泥的无聊段落。

sentences.en: on how you mix cement.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Good Lord.
sentences.zh: 我简直可以想象范·蒂尔堡坐在办公室里，

sentences.en: I can just imagine Van Tilburg sitting in his office
sentences.zh: 梦想着让人们感到无聊的新方法。

sentences.en: and dreaming up new ways to make people bored.
sentences.zh: 总之，当你让志愿者思考一段记忆时，他们越无聊，

sentences.en: Anyway, the more bored volunteers get when you ask them to think about a memory,
sentences.zh: 范·蒂尔堡和伊古发现，无聊的志愿者最终会陷入怀旧的思考，

sentences.en: Van Tilburg and Igu find bored volunteers end up into nostalgic thinking,
sentences.zh: 怀旧的记忆。

sentences.en: nostalgic memories.
sentences.zh: 现在，我必须说，我不觉得这特别反直觉。

sentences.en: Now, I have to say, I don't find this particularly counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都见过这种情况发生。

sentences.en: Many of us have seen this happen.
sentences.zh: 但我确实想知道，这是否解释了为什么许多艺术家和创意思想家，

sentences.en: But I do wonder if this explains why many artists and creative thinkers
sentences.zh: 说无聊是一件有用的事情。

sentences.en: say that being bored is a useful thing.
sentences.zh: 无聊可以让我们处于一种开放的心态，去进行白日梦、

sentences.en: Boredom can put us in a state of mind that's open to daydreaming,
sentences.zh: 想象力和创造力。

sentences.en: imagination, and creativity.
sentences.zh: 非常有意思。

sentences.en: Very interesting.
sentences.zh: 你认为这和意义也有关系吗？

sentences.en: Do you think this has to do with meaning too?
sentences.zh: 我们感到毫无意义，所以我们回顾生活并说，

sentences.en: That we're feeling meaningless and so we go back in our lives and say,
sentences.zh: 哦，我在小联盟打出的那个精彩全垒打，或者我结婚的那一天。

sentences.en: oh, that great home run I hit in Little League or the day I got married.
sentences.zh: 不是要把这两件事等同起来，但你明白我的意思。

sentences.en: Not to equate those two events, but you get the idea.
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道，丹。

sentences.en: I just want to know, Dan.
sentences.zh: 这一段没有经过剪辑，你妻子会听到这些的。

sentences.en: This segment is not being edited and your wife is going to be hearing this.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，幸运的是，我从来没有在小联盟打出过全垒打，

sentences.en: Well, fortunately, I've never hit a home run in Little League,
sentences.zh: 所以那完全是幻想，而不是怀旧。

sentences.en: so that's a complete fantasy, not nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你是对的。

sentences.en: But I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实与无意义感有关，以及某种寻找意义的动力，

sentences.en: I think it does have something to do with meaninglessness and sort of the drive to find
sentences.zh: 以及当我们感到无聊时，我们是如何倾向于那种思考方式的。

sentences.en: meaning and how we drift toward that kind of thinking when we are bored.
sentences.zh: 好了，丹。

sentences.en: All right, Dan.
sentences.zh: 如果你准备好了，你的下一个 60 秒现在开始。

sentences.en: If you're ready, your next 60 seconds starts right now.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay, so how much do we hate being bored?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们到底有多讨厌无聊呢？

sentences.en: That's the question a team of researchers led by Timothy Wilson of the University of Virginia
sentences.zh: 这是弗吉尼亚大学的蒂莫西·威尔逊（Timothy Wilson）带领的研究团队

sentences.en: answered in the prestigious journal Science.
sentences.zh: 在权威期刊《科学》上回答的问题。

sentences.en: In 11 experiments, they confirmed that we really don't like being left alone in an empty room,
sentences.zh: 在11项实验中，他们证实了我们确实不喜欢独自待在空房间里，

sentences.en: even for just 15 minutes, with nothing but our own thoughts.
sentences.zh: 哪怕只是15分钟，除了自己的思绪外什么都没有。

sentences.en: But one of these experiments was rather shocking.
sentences.zh: 但其中一项实验相当令人震惊。

sentences.en: Researchers put participants in one of their unadorned rooms,
sentences.zh: 研究人员把参与者关进一间空荡荡的房间，

sentences.en: asked them to do nothing except think,
sentences.zh: 要求他们除了思考什么都别做，

sentences.en: but, get this, offered them the option of giving themselves painful electric shocks.
sentences.zh: 但重点来了，他们还提供了给自己施加痛苦电击的选项。

sentences.en: One quarter of the women and two-thirds of the men chose to shock themselves at least once.
sentences.zh: 四分之一的女性和三分之二的男性选择了至少电击自己一次。

sentences.en: One guy, in fact, shocked himself 190 times, which is just kind of weird.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有个家伙电击了自己190次，这简直有点不可思议。

sentences.en: In other words, simply being alone with their own thoughts for 15 minutes was so horrifying,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，仅仅是独自与思绪相处15分钟就让人感到如此恐惧，

sentences.en: so terrifyingly boring, that many preferred to harm themselves.
sentences.zh: 如此令人难以忍受的无聊，以至于许多人宁愿伤害自己。

sentences.en: Self-administering electric shocks was less painful than just being bored.
sentences.zh: 比起单纯的无聊，自我电击带来的痛苦反而更轻。

sentences.en: Wow, that is an amazing study, Dan.
sentences.zh: 哇，丹，这真是一项惊人的研究。

sentences.en: And do you know what the voltage was on these shocks?
sentences.zh: 你知道这些电击的电压是多少吗？

sentences.en: I have no idea, but I know that it was painful because they also tested,
sentences.zh: 我不知道，但我知道那很疼，因为他们也做过测试，

sentences.en: and they found out that these participants said they would pay to avoid these shocks,
sentences.zh: 结果发现这些参与者表示他们愿意花钱来避免这些电击，

sentences.en: and yet when they were bored, they brought them on.
sentences.zh: 然而当他们感到无聊时，却主动选择了电击。

sentences.en: In other words, they would actually be willing to pay even more to avoid being bored.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，为了避免无聊，他们甚至愿意花更多的钱。

sentences.en: That's what it sounds like, which just seems crazy.
sentences.zh: 听起来确实如此，这简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: So, Shankar, you're next.
sentences.zh: 好了，尚卡尔（Shankar），轮到你了。

sentences.en: Here's your 60 seconds.
sentences.zh: 这是你的60秒时间。

sentences.en: Starts right now.
sentences.zh: 现在开始。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This is one of my favorite stories about how much we hate to be bored.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的故事之一，关于我们有多讨厌无聊。

sentences.en: Richard Larson at MIT tells a story about how business passengers arriving on early morning
sentences.zh: 麻省理工学院的理查德·拉尔森（Richard Larson）讲过一个故事，关于那些清晨抵达休斯敦的

sentences.en: flights into Houston were complaining about being bored as they waited for the conveyor belt
sentences.zh: 商务旅客，他们抱怨在等待行李传送带

sentences.en: to bring their bags.
sentences.zh: 运送行李时感到无聊。

sentences.en: The airline company brought in consultants.
sentences.zh: 航空公司请来了顾问。

sentences.en: They hired baggage handlers.
sentences.zh: 他们雇佣了行李搬运工。

sentences.en: They reduced the waiting time to eight minutes max.
sentences.zh: 他们将等待时间缩短到了最多八分钟。

sentences.en: Nothing worked.
sentences.zh: 但什么都没用。

sentences.en: The complaints kept coming in.
sentences.zh: 投诉依然不断。

sentences.en: So the airline thought harder.
sentences.zh: 于是航空公司进行了更深入的思考。

sentences.en: Executives realized that business passengers were spending only a couple of minutes disembarking
sentences.zh: 高管们意识到，商务旅客下飞机只需要几分钟，

sentences.en: from the plane and six or seven minutes waiting in baggage claim.
sentences.zh: 而在行李提取处等待却要六七分钟。

sentences.en: The solution?
sentences.zh: 解决方案是什么？

sentences.en: They moved the arrival gate further from baggage claim.
sentences.zh: 他们把到达登机口移到了离行李提取处更远的地方。

sentences.en: Passengers now spent six or seven minutes walking to baggage claim and one or two minutes
sentences.zh: 现在乘客需要花六七分钟走到行李提取处，而等待行李的时间

sentences.en: waiting for their bags.
sentences.zh: 只有一两分钟。

sentences.en: Poof!
sentences.zh: 砰！

sentences.en: The complaints disappeared.
sentences.zh: 投诉消失了。

sentences.en: Extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 太绝了。

sentences.en: I mean, this goes to, there's a concept called occupied time, where if our time is occupied,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这涉及到一个概念，叫做“占用时间”，即如果我们的时间被占用了，

sentences.en: we don't feel a sense of distress.
sentences.zh: 我们就不会感到焦虑。

sentences.en: So we'll take more occupied time instead of a shorter amount of time that isn't occupied.
sentences.zh: 所以我们宁愿选择更长的占用时间，也不愿选择较短但未被占用的时间。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个观点。

sentences.en: It is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But you should never check your bags.
sentences.zh: 但你最好还是别托运行李。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So there you have it.
sentences.zh: 所以，就是这样。

sentences.en: Boredom can make you prejudiced.
sentences.zh: 无聊会让你产生偏见。

sentences.en: It can make you nostalgic.
sentences.zh: 它会让你变得怀旧。

sentences.en: Completely pointless activities can reduce your feelings of boredom.
sentences.zh: 完全无意义的活动可以减少你的无聊感。

sentences.en: But here's the most important takeaway.
sentences.zh: 但这是最重要的结论。

sentences.en: If you find yourself bored and asking yourself whether you should stick your finger in that
sentences.zh: 如果你发现自己感到无聊，并且在考虑是否要把手指伸进旁边的

sentences.en: electrical socket nearby, please don't.
sentences.zh: 电源插座里，请千万别这么做。

sentences.en: Instead, go listen to old editions of Stopwatch Science.
sentences.zh: 相反，去听听《Stopwatch Science》的往期节目吧。

sentences.en: Dan and I promise to keep you entertained.
sentences.zh: 丹和我保证会让你们感到有趣。

sentences.en: Dan, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 丹，谢谢你今天加入我。

sentences.en: Thank you, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尚卡尔。

sentences.zh: 《Hidden Brain》由卡拉·麦格克-艾利森（Cara McGurk-Allison）、玛吉·彭曼（Maggie Penman）和马克斯·内斯特拉克（Max Nestrack）制作。

sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook、Twitter和Instagram上找到更多关于《Hidden Brain》的内容，也可以在

sentences.zh: 当地公共广播电台收听我的故事。

sentences.zh: 发送邮件至hiddenbrain@npr.org订阅我们的通讯。

sentences.zh: 请务必在主题栏中写上“subscribe”这个词。

sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam），这是NPR。
